LOAD-BEARING AND VERIFIED at its single citation site, folio/quantum-observable-universe/observations/q-deformed-nuclear-models-comparison.md:7. That block attributes to the source (a) a Hamiltonian proportional to the second Casimir of SU_q(2) with spectrum E_I = (1/2 theta)[I]_q[I+1]_q + E_0, and (b) a phase deformation q = e^{i phi} with [I]_q = sin(phi I)/sin(phi) fitted per band. Both check out: the document gives H = (1/2 theta) C_2[SU_q(2)] + E_0 on pp.1-2, and on p.2 (restated p.3) treats q as a phase with the resulting sin(tau I) sin(tau(I+1)) spectrum, tying tau to the valence-pair number and the variable-moment-of-inertia softness parameter exactly as the block's critique describes. This is the good case of a contrast citation: the block uses the source to sharpen a distinction (fitted phase on the unit circle versus the framework's real q_0 > 1) and represents it accurately, without borrowing a number.

keyResults.statement: H = (1/2 theta) C_2[SU_q(2)] + E_0 with q a phase, giving the oscillatory rotational spectrum through [I]_q = sin(tau I)/sin(tau), with tau fitted per band.
